name: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
holding: Parliament cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution. Amendment power under Art. 368 is limited.

timeline_events.event: Writ petition filed challenging Kerala Land Reforms Act
13-Judge Constitution Bench constituted
Judgment delivered: 7-6 majority upholds basic structure doctrine

name: I.C. Golak Nath v. State of Punjab
holding: Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights. Constitutional amendments are 'law' under Art. 13. (Later modified by Kesavananda)

timeline_events.event: Judgment delivered by 11-Judge Bench with 6:5 majority

name: Shankari Prasad v. Union of India
holding: Parliament has power to amend any part of the Constitution including Fundamental Rights under Art. 368.

timeline_events.event: Judgment upholding First Amendment

name: Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan
holding: Parliament's amending power under Art. 368 includes Fundamental Rights. Confirmed Shankari Prasad.

timeline_events.event: Judgment confirming Shankari Prasad view

name: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
holding: Procedure established by law under Art. 21 must be just, fair and reasonable. Right to travel abroad is part of personal liberty. Arts. 14, 19, 21 form a golden triangle.
principle: Due Process / Just, Fair and Reasonable Procedure

timeline_events.event: Passport impounded by Government
7-Judge Bench delivers landmark judgment expanding Art. 21

name: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
holding: Fundamental rights are mutually exclusive. Art. 21 only requires procedure as per enacted law, not reasonableness of procedure.

timeline_events.event: First major fundamental rights case decided

name: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India
holding: Sections 4 and 55 of 42nd Amendment struck down. Balance between fundamental rights and directive principles is part of basic structure. Judicial review cannot be excluded.
principle: Limited amending power / Judicial review as basic structure

timeline_events.event: 42nd Amendment enacted during Emergency
SC strikes down key provisions of 42nd Amendment

name: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
holding: President's Rule under Art. 356 is subject to judicial review. Secularism is part of basic structure. Floor test is the only way to test majority.
principle: Judicial review of President's Rule / Secularism as basic structure

timeline_events.event: Karnataka government dismissed under Art. 356
9-Judge Bench delivers landmark on federalism and secularism

name: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
holding: 50% ceiling on reservations. Creamy layer must be excluded from OBC reservations. No reservations in promotions.
principle: Mandal Commission / 50% reservation ceiling / Creamy layer

timeline_events.event: V.P. Singh government announces implementation of Mandal Commission report
9-Judge Bench delivers judgment upholding 27% OBC reservation with creamy layer exclusion

name: I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu
holding: Laws placed in 9th Schedule after April 24, 1973 are subject to judicial review if they violate basic structure.
principle: 9th Schedule not immune from basic structure review

timeline_events.event: 9-Judge Bench holds 9th Schedule laws post-1973 are reviewable

name: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan
holding: Laid down guidelines to prevent sexual harassment at workplace until legislation is enacted. International conventions enforceable in absence of domestic law.
principle: Vishaka Guidelines / Workplace sexual harassment prevention

timeline_events.event: Bhanwari Devi gang-raped for preventing child marriage
SC lays down Vishaka Guidelines for workplace sexual harassment

name: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
holding: Laid down 11 mandatory requirements for arrest and detention to prevent custodial violence and torture.
principle: Rights of arrested persons / Anti-custodial torture guidelines

timeline_events.event: Letter petition filed highlighting custodial deaths in West Bengal
SC issues 11-point guidelines for arrest procedures

name: Hussainara Khatoon v. Home Secretary, State of Bihar
holding: Right to speedy trial is a fundamental right under Art. 21. Free legal aid is a constitutional right of every accused who cannot afford a lawyer.
principle: Right to speedy trial / Right to free legal aid

timeline_events.event: PIL filed based on newspaper reports about undertrial prisoners in Bihar languishing for years

name: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab
holding: Death penalty is constitutional but should be imposed only in the 'rarest of rare' cases. Court must consider aggravating and mitigating circumstances.

timeline_events.event: 4:1 majority upholds constitutionality of death penalty with 'rarest of rare' limitation

name: Machhi Singh v. State of Punjab
holding: Elaborated categories for rarest of rare — manner of commission, motive, anti-social nature, magnitude of crime, personality of victim.

timeline_events.event: SC elaborates 5 categories for applying rarest of rare doctrine

name: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
holding: Right to privacy is a fundamental right under Art. 21 of the Constitution. Overruled ADM Jabalpur and M.P. Sharma on this point.
principle: Right to privacy as fundamental right

timeline_events.event: Justice Puttaswamy files PIL challenging Aadhaar scheme
9-Judge unanimous bench declares privacy as fundamental right

name: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
holding: Section 377 IPC decriminalized insofar as it criminalizes consensual sexual acts between adults. LGBTQ+ community has constitutional rights to equality, dignity, and privacy.

timeline_events.event: Navtej Singh Johar files curative petition
5-Judge Bench unanimously decriminalizes consensual homosexual acts

name: Shayara Bano v. Union of India
holding: Instant triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) is unconstitutional. Struck down by 3:2 majority.

timeline_events.event: Shayara Bano files petition challenging triple talaq
3:2 majority strikes down instant triple talaq

name: Joseph Shine v. Union of India
holding: Section 497 IPC (adultery as criminal offence) struck down as unconstitutional. Treats wife as chattel of husband, violates dignity and equality.

timeline_events.event: Joseph Shine files PIL challenging adultery law
Unanimous 5-Judge Bench strikes down S. 497 IPC

name: Indian Young Lawyers Association v. State of Kerala
holding: Ban on entry of women of menstruating age (10-50) into Sabarimala temple is unconstitutional. 4:1 majority with Justice Indu Malhotra dissenting.
principle: Right to worship / Gender equality in religious practice
statutes_applied: Kerala Hindu Places of Public Worship (Authorization of Entry) Rules 1965

timeline_events.event: PIL filed challenging ban on women's entry to Sabarimala
4:1 majority allows women of all ages into Sabarimala temple

name: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak)
holding: Evolved the 'absolute liability' doctrine for hazardous industries. Enterprise owes absolute duty to community — no exceptions for due diligence.
principle: Absolute liability doctrine (Oleum gas leak case)

timeline_events.event: Oleum gas leak from Shriram Industries in Delhi
SC evolves absolute liability doctrine — stricter than Rylands v Fletcher

name: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. Union of India
holding: Precautionary principle and polluter pays principle are part of Indian environmental law under Art. 21. Sustainable development is the answer.

timeline_events.event: SC applies international environmental principles to Indian law

name: National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India
holding: Recognized transgender persons as third gender. Directed government to grant legal recognition, reservations, and rights.
principle: Transgender persons' rights / Third gender recognition

timeline_events.event: NALSA files petition for transgender rights
SC recognizes transgender as third gender, directs welfare measures

name: Aruna Ramchandra Shanbaug v. Union of India
holding: Permitted passive euthanasia with safeguards. Active euthanasia remains illegal. Set up guidelines for passive euthanasia decisions.
principle: Passive euthanasia / Right to die with dignity

timeline_events.event: Aruna Shanbaug sexually assaulted by ward boy at KEM Hospital
SC allows passive euthanasia with safeguards, rejects active

name: Common Cause v. Union of India
holding: Right to die with dignity is part of Art. 21. Legalized advance medical directives (living wills) for passive euthanasia.

timeline_events.event: Common Cause files PIL for right to die with dignity
5-Judge Bench legalizes advance directives (living wills)

name: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
holding: Section 66A of IT Act struck down as unconstitutional for being vague and overbroad, violating free speech under Art. 19(1)(a).

timeline_events.event: Two girls arrested in Palghar for Facebook post questioning Mumbai shutdown
SC strikes down S. 66A IT Act as unconstitutional

name: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India (First Judges Case)
holding: Executive has primacy in appointment of judges. 'Consultation' does not mean 'concurrence'. Any citizen can file PIL.
principle: First Judges Case / PIL locus standi expanded

timeline_events.event: 7-Judge Bench decides First Judges Case — executive primacy

name: SC Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (Second Judges Case)
holding: CJI has primacy in judicial appointments. Established the collegium system — judges appointing judges. 'Consultation' means 'concurrence'.

timeline_events.event: 9-Judge Bench overrules First Judges Case, establishes collegium system

name: ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla
holding: During Emergency, fundamental rights including Art. 21 stand suspended. Citizens have no locus standi to challenge detention. Justice Khanna's lone dissent is celebrated.
principle: Habeas corpus during Emergency (overruled by Puttaswamy)

timeline_events.event: Internal Emergency declared by Indira Gandhi
4:1 majority holds habeas corpus suspended during Emergency — Justice Khanna dissents

name: Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum
holding: Muslim divorced women are entitled to maintenance under S. 125 CrPC beyond the iddat period. S. 125 is a secular provision applying to all.

timeline_events.event: Shah Bano files maintenance petition after triple talaq
SC holds Muslim women entitled to maintenance under S. 125 CrPC

name: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation
holding: Right to livelihood is integral part of right to life under Art. 21. Pavement dwellers cannot be evicted without hearing and due process.

timeline_events.event: Bombay Municipal Corporation begins demolishing pavement dwellings
SC holds right to livelihood is fundamental right under Art. 21

name: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
holding: Right to live with dignity includes freedom from bonded labour. State must identify, free, and rehabilitate bonded labourers. PIL jurisdiction expanded.
principle: Abolition of bonded labour / Epistolary jurisdiction

timeline_events.event: PIL filed about bonded labourers in stone quarries of Faridabad
SC directs identification and rehabilitation of bonded labourers

name: Francis Coralie Mullin v. Administrator, Union Territory of Delhi
holding: Right to life includes right to live with human dignity — adequate nutrition, clothing, shelter, reading, writing, and expressing oneself.
principle: Right to live with human dignity

timeline_events.event: SC expansively interprets right to life to include dignified living conditions

name: Sunil Batra v. Delhi Administration
holding: Prisoners retain fundamental rights. Solitary confinement and bar fetters are unconstitutional. Epistolary jurisdiction through letters.

timeline_events.event: SC holds prisoners retain fundamental rights, abolishes solitary confinement

name: Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras
holding: Freedom of press is included in freedom of speech and expression under Art. 19(1)(a). Pre-censorship by State is unconstitutional.
statutes_applied: Madras Maintenance of Public Order Act 1949

timeline_events.event: SC holds freedom of press is part of Art. 19(1)(a)

name: Kharak Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
holding: Police surveillance regulations allowing domiciliary visits at night violate Art. 21. Early recognition of right to privacy.

timeline_events.event: SC strikes down police domiciliary night visits as violative of Art. 21

name: Naz Foundation v. Government of NCT of Delhi
holding: Section 377 IPC insofar as it criminalizes consensual sexual acts between adults is violative of Arts. 14, 15, 21. First judicial reading down of S. 377.
principle: First reading down of S. 377 (Delhi HC)

timeline_events.event: Naz Foundation files PIL in Delhi HC
Delhi HC reads down S. 377 for consensual acts between adults

name: Suresh Kumar Koushal v. Naz Foundation
holding: Reversed Naz Foundation. Upheld constitutionality of Section 377. LGBTQ community is a 'minuscule minority'. (Later overruled by Navtej Johar)

timeline_events.event: SC reverses Naz Foundation, re-criminalizes homosexuality

name: Lily Thomas v. Union of India
holding: MPs and MLAs convicted of offences with 2+ years imprisonment stand immediately disqualified. S. 8(4) of RPA struck down.

timeline_events.event: SC strikes down S. 8(4) RPA — convicted MPs/MLAs immediately disqualified

name: Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India
holding: Voters have right to know criminal antecedents, assets, and educational qualifications of election candidates.

timeline_events.event: SC directs disclosure of criminal records, assets, education of candidates

name: Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka
holding: Right to education is a fundamental right flowing from Art. 21. Capitation fee for medical education is illegal and unconstitutional.
principle: Right to education as fundamental right

timeline_events.event: SC holds right to education is fundamental right under Art. 21

name: Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh
holding: Right to education for children aged 6-14 is a fundamental right under Art. 21. Partly modified Mohini Jain on scope.

timeline_events.event: SC refines right to education — fundamental right for age 6-14

name: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Taj Mahal Case)
holding: Industries around Taj Mahal must switch to natural gas or relocate. Taj Trapezium Zone established to protect the monument from acid rain.

timeline_events.event: M.C. Mehta files PIL to protect Taj Mahal from pollution
SC orders 292 industries to switch to natural gas or relocate from Taj Trapezium

name: T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka
holding: Minority educational institutions have right to admit students of their choice and fix reasonable fee structure. State can regulate to prevent profiteering.

timeline_events.event: 11-Judge Bench decides rights of minority educational institutions

name: Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India
holding: 27% OBC reservation in central educational institutions is valid. Creamy layer must be excluded. Economic backwardness alone is not sufficient.
statutes_applied: Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act 2006

timeline_events.event: Central Educational Institutions Reservation Act enacted
SC upholds OBC reservation with creamy layer exclusion

name: Mithu v. State of Punjab
holding: Section 303 IPC (mandatory death penalty for murder by life convict) struck down as unconstitutional for violating Arts. 14 and 21.

timeline_events.event: SC strikes down mandatory death penalty under S. 303 IPC

name: Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra
holding: Added procedural safeguards before arrest under SC/ST Act. Required preliminary inquiry. Later reversed by review and legislative amendment.
principle: SC/ST Act — anticipatory bail safeguards (later reversed)

timeline_events.event: SC adds safeguards to SC/ST Act — sparks nationwide protests
Parliament amends SC/ST Act to nullify judgment — restores original provisions

name: Union Carbide Corp. v. Union of India
holding: Settlement of $470 million for Bhopal gas tragedy victims. Established parens patriae jurisdiction for mass tort claims.
statutes_applied: Bhopal Gas Leak Disaster (Processing of Claims) Act 1985

timeline_events.event: Bhopal gas leak kills thousands
Bhopal Gas Leak Disaster Act enacted
SC approves $470 million settlement

name: Supriyo v. Union of India
holding: 5-Judge Bench declined to legalize same-sex marriage. Held that there is no fundamental right to marry. Left it to Parliament. But recognized queer unions deserve legal protection.
principle: Same-sex marriage — no constitutional right (left to Parliament)

timeline_events.event: Supriyo Chakraborty files petition for same-sex marriage recognition
5-Judge Bench declines to recognize same-sex marriage — 3:2 on most issues

name: State of A.P. v. McDowell & Co.
holding: Courts should not test reasonableness of legislation. Manifest arbitrariness doctrine questioned. Legislative wisdom not open to judicial scrutiny.
principle: Legislative wisdom / Judicial restraint in testing policy

timeline_events.event: SC upholds AP liquor prohibition — courts shouldn't test legislative wisdom

name: Vineet Narain v. Union of India
holding: CBI must be insulated from political pressure. Established guidelines for CBI investigations. CVC given statutory status.

timeline_events.event: Vineet Narain files PIL in Jain hawala case
SC issues guidelines for CBI independence

name: Prakash Singh v. Union of India
holding: Issued 7 directives for police reforms — State Security Commission, fixed tenure for DGP, separation of investigation from law and order.

timeline_events.event: Former DGP Prakash Singh files PIL for police reforms
SC issues 7 directives for police reform

name: Lalita Kumari v. Government of U.P.
holding: Registration of FIR is mandatory under S. 154 CrPC when information discloses commission of cognizable offence. Preliminary inquiry only in select categories.
principle: Mandatory FIR registration for cognizable offences

timeline_events.event: PIL filed about police refusing to register FIRs
5-Judge Bench mandates automatic FIR registration for cognizable offences

name: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
holding: Arrest under S. 498A IPC (dowry harassment) should not be automatic. Police must follow checklist. Issued guidelines to prevent misuse.
principle: Guidelines to prevent misuse of S. 498A IPC

timeline_events.event: SC issues guidelines to prevent automatic arrests under S. 498A

name: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (Aadhaar)
holding: Aadhaar Act is constitutionally valid but struck down S. 57 — mandatory linking with bank accounts and mobile phones is unconstitutional.
principle: Aadhaar upheld with limits / S. 57 struck down
statutes_applied: Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act 2016

timeline_events.event: Aadhaar Act passed as Money Bill
SC upholds Aadhaar but strikes down mandatory linking with banks/phones

name: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (Electoral Bonds)
holding: Electoral bonds scheme is unconstitutional. Violates right to information under Art. 19(1)(a). Anonymous corporate donations to political parties held illegal.
principle: Electoral bonds unconstitutional / Right to know donors

timeline_events.event: Electoral bonds scheme notified by Finance Ministry
SC unanimously strikes down electoral bonds — orders SBI to disclose data
